        <div class="accordion-content">
          <p class="resource-description">
            Physics-based simulations using MuJoCo (Multi-Joint dynamics with Contact) for biomechanical 
            analysis, including golf swing models, pendulum systems, and multibody dynamics simulations. 
            MuJoCo provides fast and accurate physics simulation for model-based optimization and analysis.
          </p>
          <a href="models-mujoco.html" class="resource-link">View Details →</a>

          <span class="accordion-icon">+</span>

        <div class="accordion-content">
          <p class="resource-description">
            Robotics and control system models implemented in Drake, focusing on underactuated systems, 
            manipulation, and control-affine dynamics. Drake is an open-source toolbox from MIT's Robot 
            Locomotion Group that provides tools for modeling, simulation, and control of complex robotic 
            systems.
          </p>
          <a href="models-drake.html" class="resource-link">View Details →</a>

        <div class="accordion-content">
          <p class="resource-description">
            Rigid body dynamics and kinematics models using Pinocchio, including forward/inverse dynamics, 
            Jacobian computations, and constraint handling for multibody systems. Pinocchio provides efficient 
            algorithms for robot dynamics and kinematics, based on Roy Featherstone's "Rigid Body Dynamics 
            Algorithms."
          </p>
          <a href="models-pinnochio.html" class="resource-link">View Details →</a>

      </div>

        <div class="accordion-content">
          <p class="resource-description">
            Pendulum-based models and simulations that serve as simplified analogs for understanding golf 
            swing dynamics, including single, double, and multi-link pendulum systems. These models provide 
            insights into control-affine systems, drift-input decomposition, and the fundamental physics of 
            underactuated multibody systems.
          </p>
          <a href="models-pendulum.html" class="resource-link">View Details →</a>

            Biomechanics simulation models using OpenSim, a freely available, open-source software platform 
            for modeling, simulating, and analyzing the neuromusculoskeletal system. OpenSim enables building 
            and analyzing musculoskeletal models, performing inverse kinematics and dynamics, and simulating 
            movement.
          </p>

          </p>
          <a href="models-myosim.html" class="resource-link">View Details →</a>
